analyzed_vuln.description: CoverageFormat2_4::serialize uses UINT32_MAX-1 as an artificial initial `last` value, then detects a new range with `last + 1 != g`. If the serialized iterator contains glyph HB_MAP_VALUE_INVALID (UINT32_MAX), the sentinel arithmetic makes the first glyph appear contiguous (`UINT32_MAX-1 + 1 == UINT32_MAX`). The counting pass therefore does not allocate a range for it; in the filling pass `range` remains UINT_MAX and `rangeRecord.arrayZ[range].last = g` performs a wild out-of-bounds write (the reported IntType::operator= crash). The serializer neither rejects invalid glyph values nor guards `range` against the allocated `num_ranges`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A malformed font must reach GSUB SingleSubstFormat2 subsetting with at least one retained coverage/substitute pair whose remapping yields HB_MAP_VALUE_INVALID (for this PoV, through `glyph_map[p.first]` or `glyph_map[p.second]` in SingleSubstFormat2_4::subset). That invalid mapped value is propagated by the pair iterator into Coverage serialization; when UINT32_MAX is the first emitted glyph (in particular, a one-element/all-invalid iterator), Coverage selects format 2 and its `last = UINT32_MAX-1` sentinel causes `num_ranges` to be undercounted, followed by the `arrayZ[UINT_MAX]` write at CoverageFormat2.hh:106.

args: In HarfBuzz, what validation expectations apply to Coverage::serialize in harfbuzz/src/OT/Layout/Common/Coverage.hh and CoverageFormat2_4::serialize in harfbuzz/src/OT/Layout/Common/CoverageFormat2.hh? Specifically, should HB_MAP_VALUE_INVALID / UINT32_MAX be rejected, or is replacing the UINT32_MAX-1 sentinel with explicit first-element state the intended robust fix? Also note whether SingleSubstFormat2_4::subset in harfbuzz/src/OT/Layout/GSUB/SingleSubstFormat2.hh should filter invalid mapped pairs.

The crash occurs when a one-element iterator containing HB_MAP_VALUE_INVALID reaches CoverageFormat2_4::serialize. Both Coverage::serialize's format-selection pass and CoverageFormat2_4's counting/filling passes initialize last to (hb_codepoint_t)-2 and use last + 1 != g. For g == UINT32_MAX the first item falsely appears contiguous, num_ranges remains zero, and the filling pass writes arrayZ[UINT_MAX]. I am considering explicit `first` state in both serializers as the minimal generic arithmetic fix, possibly combined with filtering invalid remapping output in SingleSubstFormat2_4::subset. I need preserve intended generic serializer behavior and avoid merely masking the PoV.
